body: Did some preliminary testing and it looks good from a performance standpoint (duplicated the meshes a couple dozen times and the performance from no dither to dithered was within the background noise of the gpu usage). Visuals I believe are a notable improvement, there is still noticeable banding in lower sss settings, but honestly I think it's still better than the default by far. Do you believe there's any way to attach the dither strength to some sort of "band density" metric? where the lower the quality and the higher the scale in the project settings, then the higher the dither weight? I think that's the more complex more likely to cause issues version though, I think the simple version (and more likely to not cause problems/confusion) is to put an option in Project_Settings/Rendering/Environment/Subsurface_Scattering. Regardless, good work!

> Do you believe there's any way to attach the dither strength to some sort of "band density" metric? where the lower the quality and the higher the scale in the project settings, then the higher the dither weight?

I can divide the dither strength by the sample count; that should be straightforward. I'm not sure about modulating the dither according the SSS scale project setting though, as it seems to be a global multiplier for all materials' own SSS scale.

I might look into adding an Ultra quality option for today's high-end GPUs and Movie Maker mode (the current options were added in 2020 after all - GPUs have gotten faster since), but this should be done in its own PR. Also, I don't know what algorithm was used to calculate the blur kernels, so I'd need to know that first.

~I did see something of note with regards to viewing distance in the [Human Shaders](https://github.com/matmadness/HumanShaders) project by metmadness, they have the SSS scaling down based on distance instead of being a constant scale, this lets characters with SSS not look as smudgy in the distance, I know that's not the purpose of this PR but I would be remiss if I didn't plug the idea here xD~

Actually, that's easy enough to implement in a fragment shader, scratch that.

I do think having an Ultra setting would be nice, though I honestly wonder how much more quality you could get out of it that High and dither+TAA haven't already.
